title: Vibes versus data: necessities across the income distribution
discussion_signal: Using 2024 Consumer Expenditure Survey data, the post interprets food, shelter, utilities, gasoline, health care, and other necessities as a much larger share of spending for lower-income families. Replies connect these expenditure shares to household strain and health-cost concerns, translating distributional data into lived economic meaning.
linked_research_question: How do households experience unequal room for choice when essential spending absorbs different shares of income?
limits: The post uses selected expenditure groupings and may not reproduce the full CES table
Average consumer-unit figures do not describe every family
Audience reactions are not a representative sample
